Sustainable Development Goals
   Report 2026



          Introduction SDGR 2026

       SDG monitoring in the AI era: renewing official statistics for people, trust and sovereignty

                  I. A decade of SDG monitoring: stronger evidence, unfulfilled promises

                  II. Historic expansion of the data infrastructure: achievements and lessons

                  III. Financing shocks and AI disruption: a changing landscape for official statistics

             IV. Reinvigorating official statistics

       Way forward: anchoring official statistics in people, trust and sovereignty

      Introduction SDGR 2026

                                                  The report reviews global progress towards the
                                                         Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with
                                                            only four years remaining until the 2030
         Overview
                                                            deadline, highlighting achievements, persistent
                                                             challenges, and the urgent actions needed to fulfil
                                                            the commitment to "Leave No One Behind."

                                                         While significant progress has been made since
                                                         2015, overall implementation remains off track.
           Overall Assessment                         The report calls for immediate, coordinated, and
                                                           decisive action to accelerate progress towards
                                                            the SDGs.

                                                         Since 2015, hundreds of millions have gained
                                                      access to safe drinking water and sanitation.
          Progress in Basic Services                          Electricity access has reached 92% of the
                                                            global population, with one-third generated from
                                                     renewable sources.

                                                            Global internet access increased from 40% in
                                                   2015 to 74%, connecting billions of people to
            Digital Connectivity
                                                            education, employment, and economic
                                                                opportunities.





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 1

Since 2015, new HIV infections and AIDS-related
                                                      deaths have each declined by around one-third.
          Health Achievements                      59 countries have eliminated at least one
                                                       neglected tropical disease, while 134 countries
                                                     have achieved the child mortality reduction target.

                                                           For the first time, more than half of the world's
                                                          population is covered by social protection
           Social Protection & Disaster Resilience
                                                      systems, while disaster-related deaths have
                                                                      fallen by 65% compared to the previous decade.

                                                            Global SDG monitoring has improved significantly,
                                                             with a database containing around 3 million data
         Improvement in SDG Data Systems                points, compared to limited data availability in
                                                            2015, enabling better monitoring, accountability,
                                                   and evidence-based policymaking.

                                                     Of the 139 SDG targets with measurable historical
                                                                trends, only 36% are on track or making
          Progress Towards SDG Targets                moderate progress, 49% are progressing too
                                                                 slowly, and 15% have regressed below 2015
                                                          baseline levels.

                                                    Around 1 in 10 people continue to live in extreme
           Persistent Poverty & Hunger                     poverty, while 2.3 billion people experience food
                                                               insecurity, remaining well above 2015 levels.

                                                          Approximately 2.1 billion people (one in four
                                                                globally) lack access to safely managed drinking
         Water & Nutrition Challenges
                                                           water, while over 150 million children remain
                                                        stunted due to chronic malnutrition.

                                                       Maternal mortality remains nearly three times
                                                         higher than the global SDG target, and one in five
          Health & Social Inequality
                                                      people worldwide continues to experience
                                                                 discrimination, limiting equal opportunities.

                                                                      In 2025, global temperatures reached 1.43°C
                                                  above pre-industrial levels, while atmospheric
          Climate Crisis                            CO₂ concentrations reached their highest level
                                                                   in two million years, intensifying climate-related
                                                                        risks.

                                                                Violent conflicts reached their highest levels in
                                                      decades, leading to the forcible displacement of
           Conflict & Displacement
                                                            118 million people and reversing years of
                                                      development gains.

          Decline in Development Finance                     Official Development Assistance (ODA) declined
                                                    by a record 23% in 2025, even as the annual
                                          SDG financing gap for developing countries





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 2

remained around US$4 trillion, while global
                                                                      military expenditure reached record highs.

                                                  The report emphasises closing the SDG financing
                                                 gap through reforms in the international financial
         Key Priorities for Action
                                                               architecture, debt relief, and expanding access
                                                                  to affordable finance.

                                                                                                   It calls for rapid implementation of the Sevilla
                                                Commitment on financing and the Medellín
          Global Commitments
                                                 Framework for strengthening data systems to
                                                       improve support for vulnerable communities.

                                                        Addressing challenges such as climate change,
                                                     pandemics, and global inequality requires
         Importance of Multilateralism                     stronger multilateral cooperation, with
                                                                  geopolitical tensions not allowed to undermine
                                                                   collective action.

                                                  The report reiterates that the 2030 Agenda for
                                                         Sustainable Development remains the world's
                                                    most comprehensive blueprint for peace,
         Shared Vision for 2030                            prosperity, equity, and environmental
                                                                 sustainability, urging countries to accelerate
                                                          implementation during the final four years leading
                                                                  to 2030.

    SDG monitoring in the AI era: renewing official statistics for
     people, trust and sovereignty


                                                  The report highlights the evolving role of official
                                                                   statistics in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) era,
                                                       emphasising that trusted, people-centred, and
         Overview
                                                                  nationally owned data systems are essential for
                                                            achieving the Sustainable Development Goals
                                                    (SDGs) and safeguarding the public interest.

                                                     Over the past decade, official statistics have been
                                                                            critical in responding to disease outbreaks,
         Importance of Official Statistics                  monitoring climate change, measuring poverty,
                                                            strengthening transparent governance, and
                                                           supporting evidence-based policymaking.

          Role of SDG Monitoring                   SDG monitoring has expanded global data
                                                                           availability, strengthened national statistical
                                                      systems, exposed inequalities, promoted
                                                             transparency, and enabled governments to make





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 3

better-informed policy decisions and resource
                                                                   allocations.

                                                 As the world faces interconnected challenges
                                                     such as climate change, conflicts, and other
         Growing Demand for Data
                                                               global crises, the demand for timely, reliable, and
                                                       disaggregated data has increased significantly.

                                                           Despite rising demand, financial support for
                                                             national statistical systems is declining, limiting
         Funding Challenges
                                                            the capacity of countries to generate high-quality
                                                                            official statistics.

                                                               AI is rapidly transforming how information is
                                                         generated, analysed, accessed, and consumed,
         Impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
                                                              creating both opportunities and challenges for
                                                                            official statistical systems.

                                                               AI has the potential to improve official statistics
                                                         through faster data processing, advanced
          Opportunities Offered by AI
                                                               analytics, and enhanced data accessibility,
                                                           supporting evidence-based governance.

                                                               AI systems may generate biased, inaccurate, or
                                                        misleading information, especially when
          Risks Associated with AI                       developed and controlled outside national
                                                                      jurisdictions, potentially eroding public trust and
                                                        undermining evidence-based policymaking.

                                                 As discussions begin on the post-2030
                                                    development framework, the key challenge
         Emerging Challenge                            extends beyond measuring development to
                                                       governing the systems that determine what is
                                                    measured, known, and trusted.

                                                  The report stresses that official statistics should
                                                        remain nationally owned, ensuring that countries
        Need for Data Sovereignty
                                                                    retain control over their data systems and
                                                         safeguard their data sovereignty.

                                                                      In the AI era, official statistics should prioritise
                                                         people-centred, trustworthy, transparent, and
          People-Centred Data Systems                     inclusive data systems that serve the public
                                                                    interest rather than commercial or external
                                                                     interests.

           Overall Message                               With only four years remaining to achieve the
                                              2030 Agenda, strengthening official statistical
                                                         systems, restoring investment in data
                                                                    infrastructure, and responsibly integrating AI are





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 4

essential to ensure that development decisions
                                                        remain evidence-based, credible, and trusted.

         I. A decade of SDG monitoring: stronger evidence, unfulfilled
     promises


                                                     Over the past 10 years, SDG monitoring has
                                                           created an unprecedented global evidence base
         Overview                                              for tracking progress towards the Sustainable
                                                   Development Goals (SDGs) through
                                                         strengthened official statistical systems.

                                                           Despite significant improvements in data
                                                                           availability, global progress towards the SDGs
           Overall Assessment
                                                        remains insufficient, highlighting a substantial
                                                   gap between commitments and actual outcomes.

                                                     Of the 139 SDG targets with sufficient trend data,
         Performance of SDG Targets                      only 15% are on track, while 21% are making
                                                   moderate progress.

                                                          Nearly half of the SDG targets are progressing
          Targets Lagging Behind                         only marginally or not at all, indicating that the
                                                   pace of implementation remains inadequate.

                                                    Around 15% of the targets have regressed below
          Targets Showing Regression                        their 2015 baseline, reflecting setbacks caused
                                                    by multiple global crises.

                                                  The report highlights that investments in official
                                                                     statistical systems over the past decade have
                                              made it possible to accurately measure
         Importance of Official Statistics
                                                      development progress, identify inequalities,
                                                             evaluate policy effectiveness, and support
                                                       evidence-based decision-making.

                                                         Without the strengthened data infrastructure
                                                           created through SDG monitoring, governments
                                                     would lack the evidence needed to identify areas
          Significance
                                                              of progress, address persistent inequalities, and
                                                         design effective policies to accelerate
                                                       achievement of the 2030 Agenda.

          II. Historic expansion of the data infrastructure:
     achievements and lessons





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 5

SDG monitoring represents one of the most
                                                                    significant achievements of the global statistical
         Overview                                  community, creating a shared global data
                                                                  infrastructure to measure progress towards
                                                              sustainable development.

                                                  The Inter-Agency and Expert Group on SDG
                                                             Indicators (IAEG-SDGs), through its Task Team
                                                 on Lessons Learned, highlighted that SDG
          Global Statistical Framework                     monitoring has established a common language,
                                                                 globally agreed methodologies, and a robust
                                                        evidence base for policymaking, accountability,
                                                   and international cooperation.

                                                  The number of indicators in the global SDG
                                                    Database increased from 115 indicators in 2016
         Expansion of SDG Database                        to 233 indicators in 2026, while the number of
                                                          data records expanded from approximately 3.3
                                                           lakh (330,000) to 3.2 million.

                                                            At the launch of the SDG framework, nearly 40%
                                                            of the indicators lacked internationally agreed
          Methodological Progress                               statistical methodologies. By 2026, all SDG
                                                             indicators have internationally agreed
                                                          methodologies.

                                           SDG monitoring has significantly strengthened
                                                             national statistical systems by encouraging
                                                             countries to establish SDG coordination
                                                   mechanisms, develop national reporting
          Strengthening National Statistical Systems
                                                            platforms, improve data-sharing arrangements,
                                                   and expand the use of administrative records,
                                                           geospatial information, citizen-generated data,
                                                   and other innovative data sources.

                                                  The SDG framework has driven a global capacity
                                                    development agenda, helping countries adopt
          Capacity Building                         new statistical methodologies, improve data
                                                            standards, and enhance national statistical
                                                                     capabilities.

                                                  The share of SDG indicators with good country
                                                     coverage has more than doubled, increasing
         Improved Country Coverage
                                                       from around one-third to nearly 70% over the
                                                           past decade.

          Challenges in SDG Monitoring                    Monitoring 17 Goals, 169 targets, and over 230
                                                             indicators has placed unprecedented demands
                                                   on national and international statistical systems,





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 6

requiring significant technical, financial, and
                                                                        institutional capacity.

                                                            Several SDG indicators required years of
                                                       methodological development, while others
         Measurement Challenges                       remain difficult to measure consistently due to
                                                  complex concepts, limited data availability, and
                                                            varying national capacities.

                                                  The report stresses the importance of balancing
                                                                      political ambition with statistical feasibility,
                                                          ensuring that implementation costs, technical
        Need for Statistical Feasibility
                                                               capacity, and data availability are considered
                                                           during the design of global monitoring
                                                        frameworks.

                                                           Despite overall improvements, significant data
                                                    gaps remain, particularly in measuring Gender
                                                             Equality (SDG 5), Sustainable Cities (SDG 11),
           Persistent Data Gaps
                                                         Climate Action (SDG 13), and Peace, Justice &
                                                       Strong Institutions (SDG 16), where less than
                                                           one-third of indicators have sufficient trend data.

                                              Many countries continue to face difficulties in
                                                        producing disaggregated statistics based on
                                                      income, education, disability, migration status,
          Disaggregated Data Challenges
                                                   and other socio-economic characteristics, limiting
                                                            the ability to identify populations being left
                                                            behind.

                                                            Sustainable development monitoring requires
                                                          continuous investment in statistical
         Key Lesson                                   methodologies, national statistical institutions,
                                                            partnerships, and data infrastructure, alongside
                                                                 globally agreed indicator frameworks.

                                                  The data infrastructure created through SDG
                                                           monitoring is a global public good whose value
                                                        extends beyond 2030. Strengthening this
         Long-Term Significance
                                                            foundation will be essential for future sustainable
                                                      development monitoring and for navigating an
                                                               increasingly data-driven and AI-enabled world.

          III. Financing shocks and AI disruption: a changing landscape
      for official statistics


         Overview                                 The report highlights that official statistics face a
                                                                  rapidly changing environment due to declining





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 7

financing and the rapid expansion of Artificial
                                                               Intelligence (AI), creating both significant
                                                               opportunities and emerging risks for SDG
                                                              monitoring.

                                                                  Effective SDG monitoring requires sustained,
                                                          long-term investment in national statistical
                                                      systems. However, funding has failed to keep
         Importance of Financing
                                                   pace with growing responsibilities, leaving many
                                                             countries dependent on fragmented and declining
                                                                    financial resources.

                                                                      In 2025, Official Development Assistance (ODA)
                                                            declined by 23.1% compared to 2024—the
          Decline in Official Development Assistance        largest annual decline ever recorded—bringing
         (ODA)                               ODA levels back to those seen at the beginning of
                                                            the 2030 Agenda. Further reductions are
                                                       expected in 2026.

                                                       Surveys conducted by the Inter-Secretariat
                                                   Working Group on Household Surveys indicate
                                                                   that funding cuts are already affecting national
         Impact of Funding Cuts                               statistical offices in low- and middle-income
                                                                countries, disrupting SDG monitoring, household
                                                         surveys, administrative data systems, and data
                                                         dissemination platforms.

                                                            At a time of growing global challenges such as
                                                           climate change, conflicts, inequality, and
        Need for Strong Statistical Systems             demographic transitions, countries require
                                                                      reliable, timely, and inclusive official statistics
                                                  more than ever before.

                                                               AI has the potential to improve almost every stage
                                                              of the statistical process, including questionnaire
                                                          design, survey implementation, image and text
          Role of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
                                                                  classification, error detection, quality
                                                        assurance, and making official statistics more
                                                            accessible through natural language interfaces.

                                            A meta-analysis of around 1,800 research
                                                                  articles shows that AI is already being applied
         Growing Use of AI                               across the entire survey lifecycle, demonstrating
                                                                                   its growing importance in official statistical
                                                         systems.

          Risks of AI                                         AI systems, particularly Large Language Models
                                                         (LLMs), may generate responses using outdated,
                                                               unverified, or synthetically generated data,





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 8

producing information that appears authoritative
                                                           but may be inaccurate or misleading.

                                                                      In the absence of reliable official statistics, AI may
                                                                                                              fill data gaps through extrapolation,
          Risk of Misinformation                              interpolation, or synthetic data generation,
                                                             increasing the risk of misinformation and
                                                     weakening public trust.

                                                               AI raises important questions regarding data
                                                       ownership, representation, transparency,
         Data Governance Challenges
                                                              accountability, and who controls AI systems,
                                                     making robust governance frameworks essential.

                                                  The report stresses that AI should strengthen—
                                                           not replace—the core principles of official
           Principles for Responsible AI                          statistics, including professional independence,
                                                         transparency, methodological rigour,
                                                              accountability, and protection of confidentiality.

                                                               AI and future technological innovations should be
                                                              carefully designed, well-governed, and held to
                                                            the same high standards of public trust that
       Way Forward
                                                                            official statistical systems have built over
                                                       decades, ensuring they continue to serve the
                                                               public interest.

       IV. Reinvigorating official statistics

                                                  The report emphasises the need to reinvigorate
                                                                        official statistics by placing People, Trust, and
         Overview                                     Sovereignty at the centre of statistical systems,
                                                                    particularly in the era of Artificial Intelligence
                                                                         (AI).

                                                                        Official statistics should serve people rather than
                                                         technology, ensuring that data systems are
          People-Centred Statistics
                                                                inclusive, participatory, and capable of
                                                            capturing the diversity of all population groups.

                                                                        Statistical systems should support meaningful
                                                        data disaggregation and involve communities in
           Inclusive Data Collection
                                                           deciding what is measured, how data are
                                                               collected, and how findings are used.

          Representation Gaps                      Many vulnerable groups remain underrepresented
                                                                        in official statistics. For example, only 29% of
                                                      responding countries reported statistical
                                                  programmes for internally displaced persons





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                 9

(IDPs), compared with over 70% for persons
                                                         with disabilities and youth.

                                                        Although public participation mechanisms exist,
                                                           they often fail to influence policymaking. In 2024,
        Community Participation
                                                            only 30% of rural drinking water policies reported
                                                        high levels of community participation.

                                                              Public trust is the foundation of official statistics
                                                   and depends on professional independence,
         Importance of Trust                             transparent methodologies, high-quality data,
                                                   easy accessibility, and strong confidentiality
                                                             protections.

                                                  The Statistical Performance Indicators (SPI)
                                                       improved globally from 59 (2016) to 70 (2023).
            Statistical Performance Improvement            However, significant disparities remain between
                                                     high-income and low- and lower-middle-income
                                                             countries.

                                                               AI systems rely on available data and may
                                                         generate estimates where official data are
          AI and Data Quality Risks                          missing. This can reinforce existing biases,
                                                   deepen the exclusion of underrepresented
                                                           groups, and produce misleading information.

                                                         While 93% of 167 national statistical laws (2023)
                                                             include confidentiality provisions, AI has
           Confidentiality Challenges in AI Era                 significantly increased the risk of re-identifying
                                                              individuals by combining anonymised official
                                                                        statistics with commercial and open datasets.

                                                               AI should complement official statistics by
                                                            analysing community feedback, integrating
                                                             diverse data sources (such as satellite imagery
          Responsible Use of AI                        and mobile phone data), improving
                                                              dissemination, and enhancing quality assurance
                                                            without compromising transparency or public
                                                                          trust.

                                             NSOs should remain the authoritative and
                                                                 verifiable source of official statistics by
                                                     documenting methodologies, clearly
          Role of National Statistical Offices (NSOs)         distinguishing observed data from model-
                                                      generated outputs, quantifying uncertainty, and
                                                            strengthening confidentiality safeguards before
                                                          adopting AI.

          AI Governance Principles                          AI adoption in official statistics should uphold the
                                                             long-established principles of transparency,





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                10

accountability, professional independence, and
                                                                 confidentiality, ensuring that efficiency does not
                                                            replace public participation.

                                                  The report defines data sovereignty through
                                                              three pillars: control over statistical priorities
                                                 and data, sustainable domestic financing, and
         Data Sovereignty
                                                            strong, independent statistical institutions
                                                        capable of governing national data ecosystems
                                                   and AI.

                                                 As of 2023, only around one-third of low- and
                                                      lower-middle-income countries managed their
        Weak Data Control
                                             own microdata repositories, limiting national
                                                                control over official data assets.

                                                                      In 2025, 135 countries had national statistical
                                                           plans under implementation, but only 59% were
          Financing Constraints
                                                                           fully funded. In Sub-Saharan Africa, only 15% of
                                                             countries reported fully funded statistical plans.

                                                        Although most countries legally mandate National
                                                                    Statistical Offices (NSOs) to coordinate national
            Institutional Capacity Challenges                     statistical systems, many lack the authority to
                                                       govern the broader data ecosystem required in
                                                            the AI era.

                                                        According to the 2021 Cape Town Global Action
                                                         Plan Survey, only 17% of responding countries
                                                    were satisfied with their NSO's capacity to
          Coordination Capacity
                                                            coordinate the national data ecosystem. Among
                                                       low- and lower-middle-income countries, the
                                                                 figure was only 8%.

                                                          Strong data sovereignty, adequate domestic
                                                             financing, and institutional authority are
                                                                 essential for countries to govern AI responsibly,
         Importance of Sovereignty in AI Era
                                                                audit AI systems, enforce safeguards, and ensure
                                                               AI serves the public interest rather than external
                                                                           priorities.

                                                  The report concludes that strengthening people-
                                                        centred statistics, preserving public trust, and
                                                       enhancing national data sovereignty are
           Overall Message                               fundamental for building resilient official
                                                                          statistical systems capable of supporting
                                                              sustainable development and responsible AI
                                                      governance beyond 2030.





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                11

Way forward: anchoring official statistics in people, trust and
     sovereignty

                                                  The report calls for a renewed vision for official
                                                                   statistics in the AI era, built on the three
                                                              foundational principles of People, Trust, and
         Overview
                                                          Sovereignty, to ensure that the global statistical
                                                     system continues to serve the public interest
                                                   beyond 2030.

                                                  The first decade of SDG monitoring created one
                                                              of the world's most significant global public
                                              goods—a shared statistical infrastructure that
         Legacy of SDG Monitoring
                                                          supports evidence-based policymaking,
                                                                  accountability, and sustainable development
                                                         across all nations.

                                                  The next phase should strengthen this foundation
                                                    by ensuring that official statistics remain people-
          Future Vision                                    centred, trusted, and nationally sovereign, while
                                                          adapting responsibly to emerging technologies
                                                     such as Artificial Intelligence (AI).

                                                    Governments should invest in inclusive statistical
                                                   systems that capture population diversity,
                                                      produce disaggregated data to monitor
            Priority 1: People-Centred Data Systems
                                                                     inequalities, and ensure that communities—not
                                                     algorithms—remain central to decisions on what
                                                                              is measured and how data are used.

                                                               AI adoption should adhere to the long-established
                                                                 principles of transparency, accountability,
                                                           professional independence, and methodological
            Priority 2: Building Trust in AI
                                                                 rigour, ensuring that technological innovation
                                                           strengthens rather than weakens public
                                                         confidence in official statistics.

                                                           National Statistical Offices (NSOs) should have a
                                                             stronger institutional role in governing the national
            Priority 3: Strengthening Sovereignty             data ecosystem, supported by adequate
                                                     domestic financing, enabling countries to shape
                                                                       their own AI-enabled data future.

                                             NSOs should remain the authoritative custodians
                                                              of official statistics, guiding the responsible
          Role of National Statistical Offices (NSOs)
                                                          adoption of AI, coordinating national data
                                                         systems, and safeguarding the public interest.





Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026                                                                                                12

The report emphasises that the fundamental
                                                                 principles of official statistics—impartiality,
                                                         transparency, professional independence,
         Core Principles Remain Relevant
                                                       methodological accountability, and public
                                                  access—are even more important in the AI era
                                                          than before.

                                                           Rather than creating a new normative framework,
                                                             countries should focus on strengthening
        Need for Implementation Rather Than New         institutional capacity, ensuring sustainable
           Principles                                         financing, and demonstrating the political
                                                 commitment needed to effectively implement the
                                                                  existing principles of official statistics.

                                                    Renewing official statistics beyond 2030 requires
                                                            applying these core values not only to data
                                                           production, but also to the governance of AI
            Official Statistics Beyond 2030                 systems, coordination of national data
                                                     ecosystems, and ensuring that the benefits of
                                                              technological innovation are shared equitably
                                                         across society.
